item.title: Stock futures rebound to start shortened week after tech rout: Live updates
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: original reporting, concrete detail

U.S. equity futures bounced on Sunday, as a shortened week on Wall Street got underway after all three major averages ended Friday in correction territory.

Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 353 points, or 0.7%. S&P 500 futures added 1.3%, and Nasdaq-100 futures rose 2.3%.

Last week, the major indexes tumbled as worries about the artificial intelligence trade continued to spook investors, despite Anthropic's record debut on Thursday.

By the end of the rout last week — which was the worst weekly decline for the Nasdaq Composite and Dow in more than six years, and the largest for the S&P 500 since April 2025 — all three of the major averages were in correction territory, and the Nasdaq turned negative for the year.

The Nasdaq-100 index ended Friday in bear market territory on an intraday basis, but was just shy of that mark based on the decline from its closing high on Oct. 6.

Investors this week will get a breather, no matter what price action looks like. Markets are closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday, and Friday's session will be shortened with the closing bell set to ring at 1:00 p.m.

All eyes are set to be on the shaky tech trade, as investors examine if last week's sell-off represented the market finding a durable bottom, or if equities have more room to fall.

Drew Pettit, chief investment strategist at Roundhill, said in an appearance on CNBC's "Closing Bell: Overtime" on Friday that the indiscriminate selling at the end of the week — which extended beyond just tech — is a sign the sell-off may be concluding. But, he said the burden of proof is on the bulls to undermine the bearish sentiment dominating the market.

"Fundamentally, I think the floor is a lot higher," he said about how low equities could go. "Technically… you need a string of catalysts for the bulls to prove the long-term earnings story isn't broken."

Source: CNBC Top | Published: 2026-11-22 23:20 UTC | Difficulty: 60/100

Original link: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/22/stock-market-today-live-updates.html

'Danger seems greater all the time': Ukrainians search for missing after Russian strikes

Several bodies have been recovered from the site of a residential building that was hit by a Russian strike in the Kyiv region, Ukraine's State Emergency Services said.

The attack early on Sunday morning in the village of Dymer killed six people, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said. Six people were injured, while others are still missing.

Continued warnings of further drone threats near the site have hampered efforts, the service added, but some people were successfully evacuated earlier in the day.

"We are living a nightmare... only God knows when it will end," one woman told the BBC's Sarah Rainsford, who's reporting from Ukraine's Kyiv region.

item.title: Mets reportedly agree $450m contract with Tarik Skubal, richest deal for pitcher in MLB history
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: original reporting, concrete detail

The New York Mets look to have sealed the biggest deal of MLB’s offseason by signing free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal.

The New York Post’s Jon Heyman reported that the deal is worth $450m over nine years, the largest contract for a pitcher in baseball history. The previous record was for the $325m, 12-year deal Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers in 2024.

The left-hander, a two-time Cy Young winner, is one of the best pitchers in baseball. He turned 30 last week, and had surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow in May, but was still a prized target for teams looking to contend in the coming seasons. He reportedly also met with the Toronto Blue Jays, San Diego Padres and Los Angeles Dodgers.

Skubal’s agreement reportedly includes a full no-trade clause and a $45m signing bonus that is shielded from the management lockout that threatens the 2027 season.

Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA in 88 starts over the last four seasons, striking out 655 and walking 95 in 546 innings. Over his seven-year major league career, Skubal is 66-44 with a 3.02 ERA. Skubal made his MLB debut for the Detroit Tigers and remained at the club until he was traded to the Dodgers this summer.

The Mets have become one of the biggest spending teams in MLB under billionaire owner Steve Cohen. In 2024, they signed Juan Soto to a deal worth $765m, the richest contract in sports history.

Despite their spending, the Mets have missed the playoffs for the last two seasons. 2026 was particularly disappointing as they finished bottom of the NL East despite having MLB’s highest payroll on opening day.

Last week, MLB commissioner Rob Manfred insisted owners will not budge from their demand for a salary cap, something which would hit a Mets team carrying both the salaries of Soto and Skubal.

The Mets sealed another long-term deal on Saturday, signing 22-year-old center fielder AJ Ewing to an eight-year, $95m contract.

Source: The Guardian US | Published: 2026-11-22 22:25 UTC | Difficulty: 60/100
